| **Hide Editor** (`right-panel-hide`) | Editor title bar (tab strip), after Maximize/Restore | Closes the editor content and keeps the detail (→ *Detail only*). Always shown and always enabled, regardless of whether a detail panel is currently visible. |

| **Show Editor** (`right-panel-show`) | Editor title bar (tab strip), same slot as Hide Editor | Reveals the (possibly empty) editor content again. Always shown whenever the editor area is closed, regardless of the active tab's detail support. |
| **Collapse All Diffs** | Changes editor header, primary inline | Collapses every file in the Changes multi-diff (`SessionChangesEditor.collapseAllDiffs`). |

Restored managed Changes/Files tabs are inserted at the **end** of the tab strip. Search opens a new Search editor and is unavailable for Quick Chats; it is offered only from this menu (and the Command Palette), not in the empty editor group's Add Tab list or the Session Activity Bar. **Hidden when the editor area is closed.** |

| **Toggle Side Panel** | Command / keybinding | Closes/opens the **whole** side pane (editor + detail together) → chat-only and back. The mechanics live on the workbench layout service (`toggleSidePane`); while the editor area is maximized, the shared `Workbench.toggleSidePane()` remembers maximization, un-maximizes, then performs the collapse so the restored detail is also hidden. Reopening restores the complete side-pane composition before re-maximizing the editor. Hiding a focused side pane moves focus to the sessions list. |

| **Toggle Sessions List** | Title bar / command | Collapses/opens the left sessions list. Collapsing it gives the freed width to the editor/detail side pane (not the chat); reopening restores the previous editor/detail width so the chat gets that space back. No desktop editor or detail action changes this visibility. |

| **Grid sash** | Between the chat and the third pane | Dragging the side pane never changes Details visibility. Details keeps its minimum width while editor content yields and eventually collapses under width pressure. Dragging a detail-only side pane wider keeps the editor content closed. Double-clicking with Details visible preserves the current Details width and splits all remaining width equally between chat and editor content, with no 600px cap. Grid minimum widths take precedence in narrow layouts. Hiding Details after a reset leaves the chat/side-pane boundary unchanged and returns the Details width to Editor content. With Details hidden the sash uses the native equal split, and in detail-only mode it resets Details to 300px. |

**Reopening after lifecycle cleanup.** If lifecycle work force-closes every tab, the whole side pane can close; when it reopens, a New Session re-ensures the managed Changes and Files tabs, while an Existing Session shows the empty group with the Add Tab actions (Detail only still ensures both).

-**Session Toolbar.** A vertical icon-only toolbar is docked at the right edge of the active chat view, below its tab row or session header. While it is enabled, every chat group showing an existing chat insets its transcript and input equally on both sides (active or not, so focusing another chat does not shift its content), so the content stays centered with even space beside it and never runs under the toolbar. Each such chat group has its own toolbar, but only the active chat of the active session shows it. The new-session view (including while a new session is being prepared) and the new-chat view neither show it nor reserve room for it. Users can drag it up and down by the grip at its top within the chat area; each view keeps its own position for the window's lifetime, and double-clicking the grip restores the default. It offers Changes, Files, Browser, and Canvas — each only when that tab is available, not based on whether the tab is currently open. It stays visible whether the side pane is open or closed. Choosing an entry opens or activates its tab; when the side pane is closed, this reveals it through the normal reveal-on-open path. The toolbar is hidden when it has no entries and in the phone layout. Users can turn it off with the `sessions.showSessionToolbar` setting or the **View > Appearance > Session Toolbar** toggle.

+**Session Activity Bar.** A vertical icon-only activity bar is docked at the right edge of the active chat view, below its tab row or session header. While it is enabled, every chat group insets its transcript and input equally on both sides (active or not, so focusing another chat does not shift its content), so the content stays centered with even space beside it and never runs under the activity bar. Each chat group has its own activity bar, but only the active chat of the active session shows it. It shows beside existing chats, the new-chat view, and the new-session view (including while a new session is being prepared). Users can drag it up and down by the grip at its top within the chat area; each view keeps its own position for the window's lifetime, and double-clicking the grip restores the default. It offers Changes, Files, Browser, and Canvas — each only when that tab is available, not based on whether the tab is currently open. Its layout actions frame them, each set apart by a separator: **Toggle Side Panel** above and **Show/Hide Panel** below. While the layout actions show, those two toggles leave the title bar; the phone layout, which has no Session Activity Bar, keeps them in the title bar. The layout actions are controlled by the `sessions.sessionActivityBar.showLayoutActions` setting (off by default) or the **Show Layout Actions** toggle in the activity bar's context menu. It stays visible whether the side pane is open or closed. Choosing an entry opens or activates its tab; when the side pane is closed, this reveals it through the normal reveal-on-open path. The activity bar is hidden when it has no entries and in the phone layout. Users can turn it off with the `sessions.showSessionActivityBar` setting or the **View > Appearance > Session Activity Bar** toggle.

**Side-pane-closed persists across reload.** Closing the whole side pane is remembered across a window reload. On reload the restored managed tab does **not** re-reveal the detail: the detail-panel forced reveal is gated on the editor content being visible, so a fully-closed side pane stays closed until the user reopens it.
